svg.title: Base-and-limit and page translation answer different questions
svg.desc: Two separate illustrative examples compare an upward-growing segment model with paging. For a one-byte segment access, offset 0x234 is below inclusive limit 0x1FFF, and adding base 0x00400000 yields linear address 0x00400234; offset 0x2000 is out of range. With 4 KiB pages, separate virtual address 0x4234 selects virtual page 4 and offset 0x234. A page-table entry maps page 4 to frame base 0x001A0000, producing physical address 0x001A0234. Flat Windows segments do not replace page mapping and protection.
svg.metadata: Original geometric teaching artwork authored for Game Hacking Academy, 2026-10-09. Public domain dedication: CC0 1.0 Universal, https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/. Concept and illustrative values belong to site/src/content/docs/pages/11/06.mdx. No third-party image assets. Diagram dimensions and placements are schematic.
svg.text: Segments and pages answer different questions
Conceptual segment: a base and an inclusive limit
A one-byte access at offset 2000 is outside the segment.
Modern Windows normally uses flat address segments,
then pages supply mappings and memory permissions.
